item.title: Moadim 20: Harvesting (קוצר) and Threshing (דש) on Yom Tov
item.description:
Which of the food-preparation melakhot remain forbidden on Yom Tov? The first six, from reaping and threshing to winnowing, are mostly the same as Shabbat. Removing peas from their pods by hand is allowed, but squeezing olives and grapes is not, and Rav Ovadia Yosef rules against squeezing oranges for juice.
Daily Halacha — Moadim Dayan Daniel Kada

item.title: Moadim 21: Selecting (בורר) on Yom Tov
item.description:
How does Borer, selecting, differ on Yom Tov? On Shabbat you may only remove the unwanted from the wanted, by hand, for immediate use. On Yom Tov you may select for any time that day, but not with a specialised tool such as a sieve or strainer, which looks like industrial work.
Daily Halacha — Moadim Dayan Daniel Kada

item.title: Moadim 45: The Three Weeks Part 6: Haircuts, Showers, Laundry, Meat and Wine
item.description:
What are the Nine Days restrictions this year, with Tisha BeAv on Shabbat? Meat and wine are forbidden by the Gemara only at the last meal, but the Shulhan Arukh records three customs, and most Sephardim keep all nine days. Haircuts, laundry and showers are permitted for Sephardim, as there is no week of Tisha BeAv.
Daily Halacha — Moadim Dayan Daniel Kada
